t: Charles I inherited Castile and Aragon in 1516 and became Emperor Charles V in 1519, uniting vast lands in Europe and the Americas.
American silver, the tercios and a council-based government made it Europe’s leading power, especially under Philip II.
War, debt and revolts brought decline after 1640; the childless Charles II’s death in 1700 passed the throne to the Bourbons.
dyk: Philip II governed his empire largely on paper, reading and annotating thousands of reports in his own hand from his study, and built the Escorial as palace, monastery and royal tomb.
ev: Charles I inherits the crowns of Castile and Aragon
Charles is elected Holy Roman Emperor; Cortés begins the conquest of Mexico
Charles V abdicates; Philip II becomes king
The Holy League defeats the Ottoman fleet at Lepanto
Philip II becomes king of Portugal
The Spanish Armada fails against England
Charles II dies, leaving the throne to Philip of Anjou

f.founder: Charles I of Spain (Emperor Charles V)
f.predecessor: Crown of Castile; Crown of Aragon
